html:
Niko Pirosmani was a self taught painter, born in 1862 in the village of Mirzaani in Kakheti, whose pictures of Georgian feasts, animals and people made him the best known Georgian artist.

He lived poor in Tbilisi, painting signs and pictures for taverns, often on black oilcloth, in return for food and drink. His feasts of men at long tables, his deer, giraffes and portraits of actresses have a calm, direct style. Russian avant garde artists discovered him in 1912 and exhibited his work, but he died in poverty in 1918. His fame grew in Soviet times, and a popular song about his love for a French actress spread his legend. His paintings now fill the National Gallery of Georgia. He is often compared to the French naive painter Henri Rousseau.
